# std.lazy

Range-update helpers that are not segment trees: `Flip`, `LazyTreap`, `LazyForest`, `SeqFold`, `Rope`. Range apply on a segment tree is `SegTree(op, a, act:)` (`segtree.cp`).

In prelude (no `use` needed): `Flip`.

## `struct Flip<T>(pub now: T, pub flipped: T)`

Paired aggregate `(now, flipped)` for range-toggle / complement updates (`SegTree(op, a, act: flip)`).

- `fn of(on: Bool, x: T, id: T) -> Flip<T>` — \(O(1)\); The leaf for one element that is currently `on` or off: `Flip(x, id)` when `on`, else `Flip(id, x)`.
- `fn op<M>(m: M) -> Monoid<Flip<T>>` — \(O(1)\); The monoid on pairs that folds both halves with `m` independently: `op(a, b) == Flip(m(a.now, b.now), m(a.flipped, b.flipped))`, identity `Flip(id, id)` with `id` from `Monoid.of(m)`.; traps: never (an `m` without a known identity is a compile-time error)

## `struct LazyTreap<T, F>(apply_fn: (T, Int, F) -> T, split_fn: (F, Int) -> (F, F), compose_fn: (F, F) -> F, before_fn: (T, T) -> Bool, mirror_fn: (F, Int) -> F)`

Arena-backed randomized treap with subtree-size-aware lazy tag propagation.

Fields: `apply_fn: (T, Int, F) -> T,`, `split_fn: (F, Int) -> (F, F),`, `compose_fn: (F, F) -> F,`, `before_fn: (T, T) -> Bool,`, `mirror_fn: (F, Int) -> F,`.

## `struct ForestSeq`

One sequence of a `LazyForest`, from `seq()` or `split_at`.

Fields: `id: Int`.

## `struct LazyForest<T, F>`

Many `LazyTreap` sequences in one shared node pool, so splitting one in two or appending one onto another is \(O(\log n)\) expected, where two separate treaps' `split_at`/`splice_back` copy the smaller side.

- `fn new(apply: (T, Int, F) -> T, compose: (F, F) -> F, split: (F, Int) -> (F, F) = (f, _) => (f, f), mirror: (F, Int) -> F = (f, _) => f) -> LazyForest<T, F>` — \(O(1)\); A forest with no sequences, with the tag operations its lazy updates use (see `LazyTreap.new`).
- `fn seq(mut self) -> ForestSeq` — \(O(1)\); A new empty sequence.
- `fn len(self, s: ForestSeq) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of elements in `s`.; traps: when `s` is not from this forest
- `fn push(mut self, s: ForestSeq, x: T)` — \(O(\log n)\) expected; Append `x` to the end of `s`.; traps: when `s` is not from this forest, or the forest reaches `2^31` nodes
- `fn split_at(mut self, s: ForestSeq, k: Int) -> ForestSeq` — \(O(\log n)\) expected; Split off positions `k..len` of `s` into a new sequence and return it; `s` keeps `0..k`.; traps: when `k < 0` or `k > len(s)`
- `fn append(mut self, s: ForestSeq, other: ForestSeq)` — \(O(\log n)\) expected; Move every element of `other` onto the end of `s`, in order, leaving `other` empty.; traps: when `other` is `s`, or either is not from this forest
- `fn apply(mut self, s: ForestSeq, r: Range<Int>, f: F)` — \(O(\log n)\) expected; Tag the elements at positions `r` of `s` with `f`.; traps: unless `0 <= r.lo <= r.hi <= len(s)`
- `fn reverse(mut self, s: ForestSeq, r: Range<Int>)` — \(O(\log n)\) expected; Reverse the elements at positions `r` of `s`.; traps: unless `0 <= r.lo <= r.hi <= len(s)`
- `fn get(mut self, s: ForestSeq, pos: Int) -> T` — \(O(\log n)\) expected; The element at 0-based position `pos` of `s`, with its pending tags applied.; traps: when `pos < 0` or `pos >= len(s)`
- `fn to_list(self, s: ForestSeq) -> List<T>` — \(O(n)\); Every element of `s` in order, with pending tags applied.; traps: when `s` is not from this forest

## `struct Rope<D, T>`

Implicit-key rope over a domain `D` supporting \(O(\log n)\) expected cut, paste, reverse, range tag `apply`, path queries, and point `get`.

- `fn new(a: ?[D]T = None, fill: ?T = None, merge: ?((T, T) -> T) = None) -> Rope<D, T>` — \(O(\lvert D \rvert)\); A rope over `D` holding the values of `a`, or `fill` at every position.; traps: when neither or both of `a` and `fill` are given
- `fn apply(mut self, r: Range<D>, tag: T)` — \(O(\log n)\) expected; Apply `tag` to every value at positions `r`: each becomes `merge(tag, x)`, or `tag` when no `merge` was given.; traps: when a non-empty `r` reaches outside `D`
- `fn reverse(mut self, r: Range<D>)` — \(O(\log n)\) expected; Reverse the order of the values at positions `r`; pending tags stay with their values.; traps: when a non-empty `r` reaches outside `D`
- `fn get(mut self, i: D) -> T` — \(O(\log n)\) expected; The value currently at position `i`, with pending tags merged in.; traps: when `i` is outside `D`
- `fn query_path<R>(mut self, i: D, f: (mut T) -> ?R) -> ?R` — \(O(\log n)\) expected calls of `f`; The first `Some` that `f` gives on the pieces holding position `i`'s value, oldest first: the value stored at `i`, then each tag still pending above it, without pushing any tag down.; traps: when `i` is outside `D`
- `fn set(mut self, i: D, x: T)` — \(O(\log n)\) expected; Overwrite the value currently at position `i` with `x`, replacing any pending tags on it.; traps: when `i` is outside `D`
- `fn to_array(self) -> [D]T` — \(O(\lvert D \rvert)\); The current values in position order, with every pending tag and reversal merged in as it walks; it reads the tree and writes nothing back.

## `struct SeqFold<T, F = Int, E = T>(m: Monoid<T>, act: ?Action<T, F>, mirror: ?(T -> T), lift: E -> T)`

A sequence of `T` that folds any run with a monoid, under lazy range tags and range reversal: an implicit treap whose nodes keep each subtree's fold in both directions, so `reverse` is a swap of the two even when `op` does not commute.

Fields: `val: List<E>`, `own: List<?F>`, `fwd: List<T>`, `bwd: List<T>`, `tag: List<?F>`, `rev: List<Bool>`, `rng: Rng`.

- `fn new<M, S: Seq<E>>(op: M, xs: S = List<E>(), act: ?Action<T, F> = None, mirror: ?(T -> T) = None, lift: E -> T = x => x) -> SeqFold<T, F, E>` — \(O(n)\) expected; The sequence `xs` folded with `op`, a bare operator (`+`, `*`, `min`, `max`, ...) or a `Monoid(id, op)`, which need not commute.
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of elements.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Whether the sequence has no elements.
- `@get fn items(self) -> yields T` — \(O(n)\) to make, \(O(1)\) per step; Each element in position order, with every tag and reversal applied; the treap is unchanged.
- `@get fn total(self) -> T` — \(O(1)\); The fold of every element in order, with every tag and reversal applied.
- `fn push(mut self, x: E)` — \(O(\log n)\) expected; Append `x` at the end.
- `fn insert_at(mut self, pos: Int, x: E)` — \(O(\log n)\) expected; Insert `x` so that it becomes the element at position `pos`; `pos == len` appends.; traps: when `pos < 0` or `pos > len`
- `fn insert_many<S: Seq<E>>(mut self, pos: Int, xs: S)` — \(O(k + \log n)\) expected for `k` new elements; Insert `xs`, in order, before position `pos` (`pos == len` appends): they take positions `pos..pos + xs.len` and later elements move up by `xs.len`.; traps: when `pos < 0` or `pos > len`
- `fn erase_range(mut self, r: Range<Int>)` — \(O(\lvert r \rvert + \log n)\) expected; Remove the elements at positions `r`; later elements move down by `r.len`.; traps: when a non-empty `r` reaches outside `0..len`
- `fn split_at(mut self, k: Int) -> SeqFold<T, F, E>` — \(O(\mathit{len} - k + \log n)\) expected; Split off the elements at positions `k..len` into a new sequence with the same monoid and action, and return it; `self` keeps positions `0..k`.; traps: when `k < 0` or `k > len`
- `fn splice(mut self, pos: Int, mut other: SeqFold<T, F, E>)` — \(O(m + \log n)\) expected for `m` moved elements; Move every element of `other` into `self` before position `pos`, in order, leaving `other` empty.; traps: when `pos < 0` or `pos > len`
- `fn get(mut self, pos: Int) -> T` — \(O(\log n)\) expected; The element at position `pos`, with every tag and reversal applied.; traps: when `pos < 0` or `pos >= len`
- `fn fold(mut self, r: Range<Int>) -> T` — \(O(\log n)\) expected; The fold of the elements at positions `r`, in order.; traps: when a non-empty `r` reaches outside `0..len`
- `fn apply(mut self, r: Range<Int>, f: F)` — \(O(\log n)\) expected; Apply tag `f` to every element at positions `r`.; traps: when the sequence was built without `act:`, or a non-empty `r` reaches outside `0..len`
- `fn reverse(mut self, r: Range<Int>)` — \(O(\log n)\) expected; Reverse the order of the elements at positions `r`.; traps: when a non-empty `r` reaches outside `0..len`

## Functions

- `fn flip_action<T, M>(m: M) -> Action<Flip<T>, Bool>` — \(O(1)\); The range-toggle action on `Flip<T>` values over `m`: the tag is a `Bool`, `true` swaps `now` and `flipped`, `false` is the identity, and tags compose by exclusive or.

## Example

```cp
let f = Flip.of(true, 10, 0)
print(f.now, f.flipped)
// output: 10 0
```
